title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.

analysis.description: The paper explores the use of sliding ferroelectric mechanisms to construct 2D sliding ferroelectric memories and synapses, employing rhombohedral-stacked bilayer molybdenum disulfide. It demonstrates the devices' performances including memory windows, conductance ratios, and flexibility, and presents their applications in neuromorphic computing and image recognition.

type.justification: The paper presents experimental results and demonstrations of the sliding ferroelectric memories and synapses, including device performance metrics and applications in image recognition.
type.quote: Here, we demonstrate the rewritable, non-volatile memory devices at room-temperature utilizing a two-dimensional (2D) sliding ferroelectric semiconductor of rhombohedral-stacked bilayer molybdenum disulfide.

name.justification: The paper focuses on demonstrating synapse-specific plasticity and image recognition using sliding ferroelectric memories, which are key elements in neuromorphic computing.
name.quote: Our work demonstrates the sliding ferroelectric memories and synaptic plasticity on both rigid and flexible substrates, highlighting the great potential of sliding ferroelectrics for emerging technological applications in brain-inspired in-memory computing, edge intelligence and energy-efficient wearable electronics.

name.justification: The research heavily involves materials science concepts, examining the properties and applications of sliding ferroelectric materials.
name.quote: Ferroelectric materials with switchable electric polarization hold great promise for a plethora of emergent applications... Recent advances have uncovered an exotic sliding ferroelectric mechanism.

name.justification: The application of a CNN for image recognition using the sliding ferroelectric synapses suggests a strong intersection with machine learning.
name.quote: Finally, we construct a five-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) based on flexible sliding ferroelectric synapses and achieve an accuracy as high as 97.81% in the recognition of MNIST handwritten-digit images.

name.justification: The paper specifically discusses constructing a CNN for image recognition tasks using sliding ferroelectric synapses.
name.quote: Finally, we construct a five-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) based on flexible sliding ferroelectric synapses and achieve an accuracy as high as 97.81% in the recognition of MNIST handwritten-digit images.

is_contributed.justification: The CNN is a standard model used for image recognition and not a novel contribution in this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Finally, we construct a five-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) based on flexible sliding ferroelectric synapses.

is_executed.justification: The CNN is implemented to perform image recognition tasks on the MNIST dataset within the study.

is_compared.quote: The weights in convolutional kernel and fully-connected layer are quantized to 32 levels and transferred to flexible sliding ferroelectric synapses for subsequent edge inference task of MNIST handwritten-digit image recognition.
